title: Repair before replacing
description: Clothing repair, mending and caring for tools
body:
A small tear can become a reason to learn about how a garment was made. Look at the fabric, the direction of the weave and the strain around the damaged area.

Keep a record of repairs: the material used, who helped and whether the repair held up over time. A community repair table can bring together people who have different skills.

Start with an object you can safely practice on. Electrical equipment and protective equipment need suitable professional guidance.

title: Living with less electricity
description: Off-grid living, energy budgets and daily routines
body:
Begin an energy notebook by listing the things you use each day. Record the purpose of each device, how long you use it and whether daylight or a simpler tool could serve the same purpose.

Compare needs before comparing equipment. Keeping food cool, reading after dark and charging a phone are different problems. A shared plan makes those differences visible.

This is a reading prompt for understanding energy needs, not instructions for wiring, generators or electrical installation.

title: A water plan for your community
description: Water access, storage records and reliable information
body:
Map the sources of drinking water that your community normally uses. Write down who publishes local water quality notices and where official emergency updates can be found.

For stored supplies, keep a clear record of the source, storage date and container instructions. Agree on who checks the supplies and how information reaches everyone.

Appearance alone cannot establish whether water is safe to drink. Follow current guidance from the relevant local water and health authorities.

title: Growing in a small space
body:
A growing space can begin with observation. Note how light moves across a balcony or window during the day, and record how much space and attention you can offer.

Choose plants suited to those conditions with help from a reliable local growing guide. A simple notebook can track planting dates, watering and changes in growth.

Neighbours can exchange observations, spare containers and seeds where local rules allow. Learning together is part of the harvest.

title: Sharing a tool library
body:
A tool library begins with an agreement about care. List the tools available, the people responsible for them and the conditions under which each tool can be borrowed.

Make the borrowing record easy to understand. Agree on return dates, maintenance and what to do when something is damaged. Do not publish private contact details in an open list.

Keep a copy of the agreement accessible to the group. Review it together as the community changes.

title: Reading a place before travelling
body:
Read a map before choosing a route. Check its date, legend, scale and the source of its information. A line on a map does not always describe present-day access.

Compare the map with current local information about transport, weather and closures. Save the information you need before leaving reliable connectivity.

A shared route plan can include meeting points and a way to communicate changes. Keep sensitive location details within the intended group.
